review_notes: Read the whole target file and the only downstream user (AnchoredIntegerIntervalsPower.lean, exists_anchored_integer_intervals_power), found by grep; the other lemmas in the file are used only inside the file. The other lemmas (anchor_power_lower, anchor_halved_power_lower, anchor_branch_lower) are already stated under the minimal real assumptions. The binder hp : 0 ≤ p in the first two follows from hm and Nat.cast_nonneg, but removing it is only an unused-hypothesis cleanup, so I did not report it. I checked the inequalities by hand and did not compile them. For the interval budget I need (p+2)^3 ≥ 2p²+6, i.e. p³+4p²+12p+2 ≥ 0. For the density budget I need (p+2)^3 ≥ 2p²+5p+1, i.e. p³+4p²+7p+7 ≥ 0. Both hold for p ≥ 0. The existing proofs only feed hp0 : 0 ≤ p to nlinarith, so the weakened statements should go through. Remaining uncertainty: whether nlinarith still closes the goals when hp : 2 ≤ p is absent. It should, because the hints use only hp0. The benefit is modest. Nothing else in the file is a useful generalisation target.

findings.excerpt: theorem anchored_interval_budget {p delta : ℝ} {m : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p)
findings.problem: Both theorems assume 2 ≤ p, but the proofs only use 0 ≤ p. The hypothesis is first turned into `hp0 : 0 ≤ p := by linarith`. Only `hp0` is passed to `nlinarith` as `pow_nonneg hp0 3` and `sq_nonneg p`, and only `hp0` is passed to the helper lemmas. The polynomial inequalities needed are (p+2)^3 ≥ 2p²+6 for the interval budget and (p+2)^3 ≥ 2p²+5p+1 for the density budget. These reduce to p³+4p²+12p+2 ≥ 0 and p³+4p²+7p+7 ≥ 0, which hold for every p ≥ 0. So the threshold 2 is an artefact of the application, not part of the mathematics. The same applies to anchored_density_budget at line 54, which has the same hypothesis and the same `hp0` step.
findings.proposed_change: Change the hypothesis in both theorems to `(hp : 0 ≤ p)`. In each proof, drop the `have hp0 : 0 ≤ p := by linarith` line and use `hp` in its place. The degenerate case p = 0 forces m = 0 and 1 ≤ delta. The statement then reads exp(-8) ≤ delta^0/40 = 1/40 in the interval budget. This is true because exp(6) ≥ 40 gives exp(-8) ≤ exp(-2)/40 ≤ 1/40. The downstream call in exists_anchored_integer_intervals_power keeps working, since it can pass `hp.trans' ...` or any proof of 0 ≤ p. It also no longer needs to carry the `2 ≤ p` hypothesis to use these budget lemmas.
findings.benefit: The budget lemmas apply to all non-negative p and are not tied to one parameter regime. A caller can use them with small p without re-proving them. The reader also sees that the constant 2 does no work in these estimates.
